name: Cyril E. King Airport
before:
The busiest airport in the US Virgin Islands and one of the busiest in the eastern Caribbean, two miles west of Charlotte Amalie on St Thomas. It handles arrivals for St John as well, and a good number of passengers heading on to the British Virgin Islands use it.

One runway and eleven gates do all the work, and the traffic mix is unusual. Across a twelve month period the airport recorded an average of 167 movements a day, of which well over half were air taxi and only fourteen per cent scheduled commercial. Small aircraft are part of the everyday picture here in a way they are not at most Caribbean gateways.

The detail worth passing on is the departure procedure. US citizens travelling to the US Virgin Islands from other US jurisdictions do not need a passport, but every passenger flying to the continental United States or Puerto Rico clears US Customs and Border Protection before boarding rather than on arrival. Build the extra time into the return.
after:
The busiest airport in the US Virgin Islands and one of the busiest in the eastern Caribbean, two miles west of Charlotte Amalie on St Thomas. It handles arrivals for St John as well, and a good number of passengers heading on to the British Virgin Islands use it.

One runway and eleven gates do all the work.

For departures, the Virgin Islands Port Authority says airline ticketing and federal services, including US Customs and TSA, may close earlier than the terminal, so build extra time into the return.

claims.note: Attributed statement, checked against the operator's own airport page. Replaces the claim that every passenger to the US mainland or Puerto Rico clears US Customs and Border Protection before boarding, which rests on Wikipedia alone (see the cut); the operator's note keeps the practical point, that departure formalities here include US Customs and can close early, without the detail no second source states. The terminal is open 6am to 11pm on the same page.

claims.claim: 167 movements a day over twelve months, well over half air taxi, 14 per cent scheduled commercial
claims.wasBefore: Across a twelve month period the airport recorded an average of 167 movements a day, of which well over half were air taxi and only fourteen per cent scheduled commercial.
claims.why: Stale: Wikipedia gives these for the twelve months ending 30 September 2017. The FAA master record no longer carries operations counts (it refers readers to the FAA's ASPM system), and the operator publishes no current count, so under the like-for-like rule a count of flights is cut rather than replaced.

claims.claim: small aircraft part of the everyday picture, unlike most Caribbean gateways
claims.wasBefore: Small aircraft are part of the everyday picture here in a way they are not at most Caribbean gateways.
claims.why: The comparison with other Caribbean airports has no source, and the point rested on the 2017 traffic mix. The operator's airline list does include small regional and seaplane operators (held back below).

claims.claim: US citizens from other US jurisdictions do not need a passport
claims.wasBefore: US citizens travelling to the US Virgin Islands from other US jurisdictions do not need a passport
claims.why: Wikipedia alone in those words; the operator's travel FAQ lists the ID the TSA accepts but does not say it. It concerns US citizens only and is of no use to UK clients.

claims.claim: every passenger to the continental US or Puerto Rico clears CBP before boarding
claims.wasBefore: every passenger flying to the continental United States or Puerto Rico clears US Customs and Border Protection before boarding rather than on arrival
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (its citation is a letter to the editor). Tried: the operator's travel FAQ and airlines page (no such statement), CBP's Know Before You Go, ports and US-citizen pages (nothing on the Virgin Islands; the port pages are drawn by script), the USVI Department of Tourism site (refused the request, 403) and the FCDO's USA entry page (no mention of the territories). Replaced by the operator's own note on departure services, attributed. Very likely true; worth restoring if a CBP or airline page can be saved.
